atlanta-ga.work: As of November 21, 2026, doctors on this list are listed at Emory, Northside and Grady hospitals, and at 9 other practices across the metro, from Marietta to Stockbridge.
atlanta-ga.plan_line: Your plan may differ. Employer self-funded plans and Medicare Advantage plans can set their own rules. Check with your plan.

insurers.name: Anthem (Georgia's Blue Cross plan)
insurers.policy: Georgia Local Prior Authorization List, updated October 1, 2026; Carelon guideline CAR15-1126.1
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: heavy bleeding, or pelvic pain, pressure or passing urine often, when not caused by infection. Approval needed; Carelon reviews it. Applies to fully insured plans and to employer plans that bought this program.

insurers.name: UnitedHealthcare
insurers.policy: Abnormal Uterine Bleeding and Uterine Fibroids (2026T0442WW), in effect November 1, 2026
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: fibroids that cause symptoms; the detailed rules are not public. Not covered when the purpose is to preserve the ability to have children.

insurers.name: Aetna
insurers.policy: Clinical Policy Bulletin 0304, last reviewed April 17, 2026
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: as an alternative to surgery to remove the uterus or the fibroids, when heavy periods, pain or pressure from the fibroids, urinary symptoms from pressure on the bladder, or pain with sex persist.

insurers.name: Cigna
insurers.policy: EviCore Peripheral Vascular Intervention Guidelines V2.0.2026, in effect November 5, 2026
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: fibroids seen on an earlier ultrasound or MRI, plus one of: abnormal bleeding (with a normal recent biopsy of the uterine lining), period pain that limits daily life despite pain medicines, pain with sex for over 6 months with no other cause, or urinary symptoms from the fibroids. Applies where EviCore manages the service.

insurers.name: Humana Medicare Advantage
insurers.policy: Uterine Fibroid Surgical Treatments (HUM-1231-005), in effect April 1, 2026
insurers.says: Covered with conditions: fibroids confirmed, you want to keep your uterus, and symptoms for 3 months or more despite medical treatment where that is appropriate.

insurers.name: Medicare (Original)
insurers.policy: National decision 20.28, Therapeutic Embolization, dated December 15, 1978
insurers.says: No specific policy; decided case by case.

atlanta-ga.medicaid_intro: Georgia Medicaid plans today are Amerigroup, CareSource and Peach State (contracts run through June 2027; the plans may change after that). None of them publishes its own policy on fibroid embolization.

medicaid.name: Peach State
medicaid.policy: Medicaid prior authorization list, effective December 31, 2025

medicaid.name: CareSource
medicaid.says: Approval needed, except when the procedure is done at an ambulatory surgery center.

medicaid.name: Amerigroup
medicaid.policy: Prior authorization lookup tool, checked twice on November 21, 2026
medicaid.says: No approval listed for an outpatient procedure with an in-network doctor. Hospital stays and out-of-network doctors always need approval. Reviews under the same Carelon guideline as Anthem.

medicaid.name: State Medicaid (no plan)
medicaid.says: Not on its list of procedures that need approval.

atlanta-ga.medicaid_checked: Checked November 21, 2026. Not needing approval is not a promise of payment; your plan's benefits still apply.
atlanta-ga.lead: Five of the six national plans in the first table cover fibroid embolization when certain conditions are met. Three of the eight Georgia plans we checked need approval before the procedure, and Kaiser needs it for some of its plans.
steps: Find your plan in the tables below.
Call the number on your insurance card. Ask whether fibroid embolization (UFE) is covered for you, and whether you need approval before the procedure.
Ask the doctor's office to check with your plan before you book.
atlanta-ga.georgia_title: Other Georgia plans: approval before the procedure

georgia.name: Kaiser Permanente Georgia
georgia.policy: 2026 small-group PPO plan document; 2026 federal-employee brochure
georgia.says: Approval needed in its 2026 small-group PPO plan document and its federal-employee plans. HMO members: call Member Services at (404) 261-2590 to ask.

georgia.name: Alliant Health Plans
georgia.policy: Prior authorization verification tool, checked November 21, 2026

georgia.name: State Health Benefit Plan, Anthem options (state employees and teachers)
georgia.policy: 2026 Anthem plan descriptions; 2027 Anthem precertification list
georgia.says: Not on the approval list in its 2026 plan descriptions. From January 1, 2027, Anthem's list names vascular embolization as needing approval. Call 855-641-4862 to confirm. On the UnitedHealthcare or Kaiser options, call (888) 364-6352 or 855-512-5997.
